news.models module¶

Database models for the News Application.

This module defines the main data structures used by the project: CustomUser, Publisher, Article and Newsletter. These models describe how users, publishers, articles and newsletters are stored in the MariaDB database through Django’s ORM.

class news.models.Article(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: Model

Represents a news article created by a journalist.

Each article has an author, optional publisher, creation date, and approval status. The approved field controls whether the article is visible through the public article API responses.

class news.models.CustomUser(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: AbstractUser

Custom user model for the News Application.

Each user must have a unique email address. Users can share the same role, meaning the system can have many Readers, many Journalists, and many Editors.

class news.models.Publisher(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: Model

Represents a news publisher.

A publisher can have many articles linked to it. Readers can also subscribe to publishers so that they can retrieve articles from selected publishers using the subscribed articles API endpoint.

news.permissions module¶

Custom permission classes for the News Application.

These permissions are used by the API views to enforce role-based access control for journalists and editors.

class news.permissions.IsEditor[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Allow access only to authenticated users with the Editor role.

Editors are responsible for approving and deleting article content.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Check whether the current user is authenticated and is an editor.

class news.permissions.IsJournalist[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Allow access only to authenticated users with the Journalist role.

Journalists are responsible for creating and updating article content.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Check whether the current user is authenticated and is a journalist.

news.tests module¶

Automated API tests for the News Application.

These tests verify that the main article API endpoints work correctly and that authentication and role-based permissions are enforced.

class news.tests.ArticleAPITestCase(methodName='runTest')[source]¶

Bases: APITestCase

Test suite for article API functionality.

The tests create sample users, a publisher, and an article. They verify authenticated access, unauthenticated access, article detail retrieval, journalist article creation, and reader restrictions.

setUp()[source]¶

Create test data used by each test case.

A reader, journalist, editor, publisher, and approved article are created in the temporary test database.

test_article_detail()[source]¶

Verify that an authenticated user can retrieve one article.

test_articles_list_authenticated()[source]¶

Verify that an authenticated user can retrieve the article list.

test_articles_list_unauthenticated()[source]¶

Verify that anonymous users cannot retrieve the article list.

test_journalist_can_create_article()[source]¶

Verify that a journalist can create an article through the API.

test_reader_cannot_create_article()[source]¶

Verify that a reader cannot create an article through the API.

news.urls module¶

URL routes for the News Application.

news.views module¶

Handle website requests and REST API operations for the News Application.

Website views support registration, article publishing, editor approval, publisher management, newsletters, and subscription filtering.

REST API views provide authenticated article retrieval and enforce role-based rules for creating, updating, and deleting articles.

class news.views.ArticleDetailView(**kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView

Retrieve approved articles and permit authorised updates or deletion.

get_queryset()[source]¶

Get the list of items for this view. This must be an iterable, and may be a queryset. Defaults to using self.queryset.

This method should always be used rather than accessing self.queryset directly, as self.queryset gets evaluated only once, and those results are cached for all subsequent requests.

You may want to override this if you need to provide different querysets depending on the incoming request.

(Eg. return a list of items that is specific to the user)
